canonical_event.name: Samsung Galaxy Note 7 Battery Recall Crisis
canonical_event.summary: Samsung Galaxy Note 7 Battery Recall Crisis was a real engineering or product-safety event involving design flaws, manufacturing defects, quality-control failure, or weak safety governance, followed by accidents, recalls, or scrutiny.

causal_relations.label: The packet-supported process links the initiating conditions through intermediate escalation/response stages to the recorded outcome or resolution.

episodes.label: Official Global Launch of Samsung Galaxy Note 7
episodes.summary: Samsung held the global launch event for its flagship Galaxy Note 7 smartphone in New York on August 2, 2016, the device was positioned as a premium high-end handset with features including iris recognition, S Pen and waterproofing, and received positive initial reviews before subsequent battery issue reports emerged.

episodes.label: First Explosion Reports Surface
episodes.summary: Between August 24 and September 1 2016, multiple reports of Samsung Galaxy Note 7 batteries exploding or catching fire surfaced globally, prompting Samsung to initiate product quality investigations and postpone shipments.

episodes.label: Global Recall Announcement Excluding China
episodes.summary: On September 2, 2016, Samsung announced a global recall of approximately 2.5 million Galaxy Note7 smartphones due to confirmed battery overheating/fire hazards linked to SDI-supplied batteries, explicitly excluding the Chinese market with the explanation that Chinese domestic units used ATL-supplied batteries with no safety defects. Following the announcement, multiple national aviation authorities including the US FAA issued restrictions on carrying Note7 devices on passenger flights.

episodes.label: Partial Recall of Chinese Market Test Units
episodes.summary: On September 14, 2016, following regulatory约谈 by China's General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine, Samsung (China) filed a recall plan covering 1858 Galaxy Note7 test units manufactured between July 20 and August 5, 2016 in mainland China; regularly sold国行 units launched on September 1, 2016 were excluded from this partial recall.

episodes.label: Domestic Explosion Incidents and Public Dispute
episodes.summary: On September 18, 2016, the first Chinese domestic Galaxy Note 7 explosion incident was reported by a user who purchased the device from JD.com, marking the start of controversy over Samsung's product safety claims for Chinese market Note 7 units.

episodes.label: Flight Fire Incident and Production Suspension Decision
episodes.summary: This episode covers the October 5, 2016 US Southwest Airlines flight Galaxy Note7 fire incident, which triggered Samsung's October 10, 2016 decision to suspend Galaxy Note7 production.

episodes.label: Permanent Production Stop and Full China Recall
episodes.summary: On October 11, 2016, Samsung Electronics announced permanent cessation of Galaxy Note 7 production and full recall of all 190,984 units sold in mainland China, concluding the prior dual-standard recall controversy for the problematic flagship device.

episodes.label: Post-Recall Litigation and Internal Investigation
episodes.summary: This episode covers post-Galaxy Note7 global recall activities including Samsung's internal investigation into battery explosion causes, pending consumer litigation cases, and preparation for the official investigation report release ahead of January 23 2017.

episodes.label: Official Release of Explosion Cause Investigation Report
episodes.summary: On January 23, 2017, Samsung held a press conference to officially release the Galaxy Note7 explosion cause investigation report, concluding the incidents were caused by battery design and manufacturing defects, and announced new battery safety measures to prevent similar recurrence.

stages.label: Product Launch and Initial Incident Emergence
stages.summary: On August 2, 2016, Samsung held a global launch event for its flagship Galaxy Note 7 smartphone in New York. The device was positioned as a premium high-end handset equipped with features including iris recognition, S Pen, and waterproofing, and received positive initial market reviews before battery safety issue reports emerged.

stages.label: Partial Global Recall and China Market Controversy
stages.summary: This stage, running from September 2 to September 30 2016, opens with Samsung's official announcement on September 2 2016 to recall approximately 2.5 million Galaxy Note7 smartphones globally due to confirmed SDI-supplied battery overheating/fire hazards, while explicitly excluding the Chinese market from the recall with the claim that Chinese domestic units used ATL-supplied batteries with no safety defects. Following the announcement, multiple national aviation authorities including the US FAA issued restrictions on carrying Note7 devices on passenger flights.

stages.label: Full Global Recall and Permanent Production Suspension
stages.summary: Triggered by the October 5, 2016 US Southwest Airlines flight Galaxy Note7 fire incident, Samsung first announced suspension of Galaxy Note7 production on October 10, 2016, followed by an official announcement on October 11, 2016 of permanent cessation of Galaxy Note7 production and sales, and full global recall of all affected devices.

stages.label: Incident Investigation and Final Conclusion Release
stages.summary: This stage runs from November 2016 to January 23, 2017, following the full global recall of Samsung Galaxy Note7, covering two core episodes: post-recall litigation handling and internal investigation, and the official release of the explosion cause investigation conclusion.
